newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firms at close after dull session.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firms at close after dull session.

text.p: The Mexican peso enhanced earlier firmness at the close on Monday, after what traders said had been a very slow session in which dealers awaited the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"It was very quiet; everyone is waiting to see what happens at the U.S. FOMC meeting tomorrow," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.4 and 1.3 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8790/7.8820 and 7.8750/7.8800 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.3 of a centavo weaker at 7.8850/7.8870 per dollar.
"I feel banks were either square or long on dollars before the session, which is why dollars were in supply," another trader said.
Dealers differed in the predictions as to whether the FOMC would raise U.S. base rates on Tuesday, although most said they expected rates to remain unchanged.
"I feel they will not raise rates, at least this time round," one trader said.
"There were reasons for rate hikes at the last (FOMC) meeting, but not now," another trader said.

Dealers said they expected Tuesday's session to be quiet, at least until the FOMC made public its decision on U.S. interest rate policy, expected shortly before the close of trade in Mexican foreign exchange markets.
